A12


The potential energy for 
\(N = 2\)
 is: 
\[E_\mathrm{p}(\alpha) = Mg \cdot y_{\mathrm{c{\cdot}m.}(0,0)} \times 4 + Mg \cdot \Delta y \times 2 \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (1)}\]
 where 
\[y_{\mathrm{c{\cdot}m.}(0,0)} = -\tfrac{\sqrt{3}l}{3}\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6} + \alpha\right) \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (2)}\]
 is the 
\(y\)
 coordinate of center of mass of triangle (0,0), and 
\[\begin{align*}
\Delta y &= y_{\mathrm{A}(0,1)} - y_{\mathrm{A}(0,0)} \\
&= -l\left[\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right) + \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} - \alpha\right)\right] \\
&= -\sqrt{3}l\cos\alpha \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (3)}
\end{align*}\]
 is the translational difference of two neighbouring triangles in 
\(y\)
-direction. Solving Eqs. (1), (2) and (3), we obtain 
\[E_\mathrm{p}(\alpha) = -\tfrac{2}{3}Mgl\left(4\sqrt{3}\cos\alpha + 3\sin\alpha\right) \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (4)}\]





A21









At equilibrium, the potential energy reaches a minimum, which gives: 
\[\left.\tfrac{dE_\mathrm{p}(\alpha)}{d\alpha}\right|_{\alpha=\alpha_\mathrm{E}} = 0 \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (5)}\]
 
\[\sqrt{3}\sin\alpha_\mathrm{E} + 3\cos\alpha_\mathrm{E} = 0 \tag*{- Eq. (6)}\]
 or 
\[\alpha_\mathrm{E} = \tan^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 point)}} \tag*{- Eq. (7)}\]





A35


If the total energy of the oscillation has the following form 
\[E(\Delta\alpha, \Delta\dot{\alpha}) = E_\mathrm{p} + E_\mathrm{k} = \tfrac{1}{2}K(\Delta\alpha)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}I(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 \text{ , \textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (8)}\]
 where 
\(E_\mathrm{p}\)
 and 
\(E_\mathrm{k}\)
 are the potential and kinetic energies of the system respectively, then the motion is a simple harmonic oscillation with angular frequency 
\(\omega = \sqrt{K/I}\)
. Here 
\(\Delta\alpha = \alpha - \alpha_\mathrm{E}\)
. Under a small perturbation, the potential energy change is: 
\[\begin{align*}
\Delta E_\mathrm{p} &\approx \frac{1}{2}\left.\frac{d^2E_\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{d}\alpha^2}\right|_{\alpha=\alpha_\mathrm{E}}(\Delta\alpha)^2 \\
&= \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{2}{3}Mgl\right)(4\sqrt{3}\cos\alpha_\mathrm{E} + 3\sin\alpha_\mathrm{E})(\Delta\alpha)^2 \\
&= \tfrac{\sqrt{57}}{3}Mgl(\Delta\alpha)^2 \ \text{\textbf{(1 point)}} \tag*{- Eq. (9)}
\end{align*}\]


The total kinetic energy of the system includes the translational kinetic energy of every plate and the rotational kinetic energy of every plate relative to its center of mass 
\[E_\mathrm{k} = \textstyle\sum E_\mathrm{k}^\mathrm{trans} + \sum E_\mathrm{k}^\mathrm{rot} \tag*{- Eq. (10)}\]
 The rotational kinetic energy is 
\[\textstyle\sum E_\mathrm{k}^\mathrm{rot} = 4 \times \tfrac{1}{2}\tfrac{Ml^2}{12}(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 = \tfrac{1}{6}Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 \ \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (11)}\]
 
\(E_\mathrm{k}^\mathrm{trans}\)
can be obtained by considering the motion of the center of mass of each triangle and setting 
\(N = 2\)
. 
\[\begin{align*}
x_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} &= m(2l\cos\alpha) + n(2l\cos\alpha)\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + \frac{l}{\sqrt{3}}\cos\left(\alpha + \frac{\pi}{6}\right), \\
y_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} &= -n(2l\cos\alpha)\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3} - \tfrac{l}{\sqrt{3}}\sin\left(\alpha + \tfrac{\pi}{6}\right). \qquad \text{\textbf{(0.5 point)}}
\end{align*}\]
 Differentiating and substituting 
\[\sin\alpha = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{19}}, \cos\alpha = \tfrac{4}{\sqrt{19}}, \sin\left(\alpha + \tfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \tfrac{7}{2\sqrt{19}}, \cos\left(\alpha + \tfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \tfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{19}},\]
 
\[\dot{x}_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} = -\left(2m + n + \frac{7}{6}\right)\frac{3}{\sqrt{57}}l\Delta\dot{\alpha}, \qquad \dot{y}_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} = \frac{3(2n - 1)}{2\sqrt{19}}l\Delta\dot{\alpha}.\]
 
\[v^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} = \dot{x}^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} + \dot{y}^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(m,n)} = \tfrac{(12m+6n+7)^2+27}{228}l^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2, \qquad \text{\textbf{(1 point)}}\]
 
\[E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k} = \frac{M}{2}\left[v^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(0,0)} + v^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(0,1)} + v^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(1,0)} + v^2_{\mathrm{c.m.}(1,1)}\right] = \frac{164}{57}Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2.\]
 
\[E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{k} = E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k} + E^\mathrm{rot}_\mathrm{k} = \tfrac{347}{114}Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2. \qquad \text{\textbf{(1 point)}}\]


Alternatively, another way to get 
\(E_k^\mathrm{trans}\)
 is based on the center of mass of the whole system: 
\[E_\mathrm{k} = \textstyle\sum E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k} + \sum E^\mathrm{rot}_\mathrm{r.c.,k} \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (12)}\]
 where 
\[E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{r.c.,k} = \tfrac{M}{2}\left[v^2_{\mathrm{r.c.}(0,0)} + v^2_{\mathrm{r.c.}(1,0)} + v^2_{\mathrm{r.c.}(0,1)} + v^2_{\mathrm{r.c.}(1,1)}\right] \tag*{- Eq. (13)}\]
 is the translational kinetic energy 
relative
 to the center of mass of the system and 
\[E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k} = \tfrac{4M}{2}v^2_\mathrm{c.m.} \tag*{- Eq. (14)}\]
 is the translational kinetic energy of the center of mass of the system.


The center of mass of each of the 2
\(\times\)
2 = 4 triangles always form diamond shape with lateral length 2
l
 cos 
\(\alpha\)
. The center of mass of the whole system is at the center of the diamond shape. Hence 
\[\begin{align*}
v_{\mathrm{r.c.}(0,0)} = v_{\mathrm{r.c.}(1,1)} &= \left.\frac{d(\sqrt{3}l\cos\alpha)}{d\alpha}\right|_{\alpha=\alpha_\mathrm{E}}\Delta\dot{\alpha} \\
v_{\mathrm{r.c.}(1,0)} = v_{\mathrm{r.c.}(0,1)} &= \left.\tfrac{d(l\cos\alpha)}{d\alpha}\right|_{\alpha=\alpha_\mathrm{E}}\Delta\dot{\alpha} \tag*{- Eq. (15)}
\end{align*}\]
 Substituting Eqs. (14) and (15) into Eq. (13), we obtain 
\[E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{r.c.,k} = 4\sin\alpha_\mathrm{E}^2\,Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 \tag*{- Eq. (16)}\]
 For 
\(E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k}\)
, 
\[v_\mathrm{c.m.} = \left.\sqrt{\left(\tfrac{\mathrm{d}x_\mathrm{c.m.}}{\mathrm{d}\alpha}\right)^2 + \left(\tfrac{\mathrm{d}y_\mathrm{c.m.}}{\mathrm{d}\alpha}\right)^2}\,\right|_{\alpha=\alpha_\mathrm{E}}\Delta\dot{\alpha} \tag*{- Eq. (17)}\]
 is the velocity of the center-of-mass of the four triangular plates, with 
\[\begin{align*}
x_\mathrm{c.m.} &= x_{\mathrm{c.m.}(0,0)} + \frac{1}{2}\left(x_{\mathrm{B}(0,0)} + x_{\mathrm{A}(1,0)}\right) \\
&= \tfrac{\sqrt{3}l}{3}\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6} + \alpha\right) + \tfrac{3}{2}l\cos\alpha \tag*{- Eq. (18)} \\
y_\mathrm{c.m.} &= y_{\mathrm{c.m.}(0,0)} + \frac{1}{2}\Delta y \\
&= -\tfrac{\sqrt{3}l}{3}\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6} + \alpha\right) - \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}l\cos\alpha \tag*{- Eq. (19)}
\end{align*}\]


Substituting Eqs. (17), (18) and (19) and into Eq. (14), we obtain 
\[E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k} = \left(\tfrac{2}{3} + 10\sin^2\alpha_E\right)Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 \ \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (20)}\]


Combining Eqs. (12), (16) and (20), we obtain 
\[\begin{align*}
E_\mathrm{k} &= E^\mathrm{rot}_\mathrm{k} + E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{r.c.,k} + E^\mathrm{trans}_\mathrm{c.m.,k} \\
&= \left(\frac{5}{6} + 14\sin^2\alpha_E\right)Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 \\
&= \tfrac{347}{114}Ml^2(\Delta\dot{\alpha})^2 \qquad \text{\textbf{(1.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (21)}
\end{align*}\]


According to Eqs. (8), (9) and (21), 
\[f = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\tfrac{\frac{\sqrt{57}}{3}Mgl}{\frac{347}{114}Ml^2}} = \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\tfrac{38\sqrt{57}}{347}\tfrac{g}{l}} \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (22)}\]
 [Note 1: 0.5 point should be deducted if there are numerical mistakes, but all steps are correct.


Note 2: A rough estimate of 
\(f\sim\sqrt{\frac{g}{l}}\)
 can get 0.5 points out of 5 points.]





B13


For arbitrary 
\(N\)
, the total potential energy 
\[E_\mathrm{p} = \textstyle\sum_{m,n=0}^{N-1}E_\mathrm{p}(m,n) \tag*{- Eq. (23)}\]
 where 
\[E_\mathrm{p}(m,n) = \tfrac{1}{3}Mg\left[y_{\mathrm{A}(m,n)} + y_{\mathrm{B}(m,n)} + y_{\mathrm{C}(m,n)}\right] \tag*{- Eq. (24)}\]
 
(0.5 points for Eqs. (23) and (24))


and 
\[\begin{align*}
y_{\mathrm{A}(m,n)} &= -nl\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \alpha\right) - nl\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right) = -\sqrt{3}nl\cos\alpha \\
y_{\mathrm{B}(m,n)} &= y_{\mathrm{A}(m,n)} - l\sin\alpha = -\sqrt{3}nl\cos\alpha - l\sin\alpha \\
y_{\mathrm{C}(m,n)} &= y_{\mathrm{A}(m,n)} - l\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right) = -\sqrt{3}nl\cos\alpha - l\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right) \tag*{- Eq. (25)}
\end{align*}\]
 
(0.5 points for all three correct coordinates)


Thus, 
\[E_\mathrm{p}(m,n) = -\tfrac{1}{3}Mgl\left[3\sqrt{3}n\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha + \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right)\right] \tag*{- Eq. (26)}\]
 and 
\[\begin{align*}
E_\mathrm{p} &= \sum\nolimits_{m,n=0}^{N-1}E_\mathrm{p}(m,n) \\
&= -\tfrac{1}{3}Mgl\textstyle\sum_{m,n=0}^{N-1}\left[3\sqrt{3}n\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha + \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right)\right] \ \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (27)}
\end{align*}\]


Using the mathematical relations 
\[\sum\nolimits_{m=0}^{N-1}1 = \sum\nolimits_{n=0}^{N-1}1 = N\]
 and 
\[\textstyle\sum_{m=0}^{N-1}m = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1}n = \frac{N(N-1)}{2} \tag*{- Eq. (28),}\]
 Eq. (27) becomes 
\[\begin{align*}
E_\mathrm{p} &= -\frac{1}{3}N^2Mgl\left[\frac{3\sqrt{3}(N - 1)\cos\alpha}{2} + \sin\alpha + \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3} + \alpha\right)\right] \\
\text{or}\qquad &= -\tfrac{1}{3}N^2Mgl\left[\tfrac{\sqrt{3}(3N-2)\cos\alpha}{2} + \tfrac{3}{2}\sin\alpha\right] \quad \text{\textbf{(1 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (29)}
\end{align*}\]


At equilibrium, 
\(\frac{\mathrm{d}E_\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{d}\alpha} = 0\)
, therefore 
\[-\tfrac{3\sqrt{3}(N-1)\sin\alpha'_\mathrm{E}}{2} + \cos\alpha'_\mathrm{E} + \cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3} + \alpha'_\mathrm{E}\right) = 0 \tag*{- Eq. (30)}\]
 
\[\alpha'_\mathrm{E} = \tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3N-2}\right) \quad \text{\textbf{(0.5 points)}} \tag*{- Eq. (31)}\]


[Remark: Increasing 
\(\boldsymbol{\alpha}\)
 lowers each triangle relative to its vertex A, but globally raises the system, i.e. the bottom tube is raised higher. When 
\(\boldsymbol{N \rightarrow \infty}\)
, the global displacement dominates, consequently 
\(\boldsymbol{\alpha \rightarrow 0}\)
.]
